title: Muffin — Pipeline
description: Is the ingestion actually working? Backlog depth, run outcomes and what each run did. Everything here comes from market.refresh_run / backlog_sample, which are SAMPLES — the live pending_* views cost ~8.4s to count (pending_prices alone is 5.4s, over the 8s statement timeout), so no panel may query them directly.

panels.title: Total work outstanding
panels.description: Every backlog added together. The shape is the question: a line that descends is draining, a flat line with successful runs underneath it is the stall this system has hit five times.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, sum(depth) as "all backlogs"
  from market.backlog_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and error is null
 group by sampled_at order by sampled_at

panels.title: Backlog depth by resource
panels.description:
Per backlog. A FLAT line here while the matching resource reports ok is the signature to recognise — see the 'backlog is not draining' alert.

IT USED TO FILTER THE INFORMATIVE CASE AWAY. Measured 2026-08-28: that filter hid 7 backlogs that had reached zero — so a queue DRAINING COMPLETELY looked identical to a series that had never existed. A panel that drops the zero row deletes exactly the state it exists to reveal — the same defect as the cross table's `limit 60`, which hid the United States because the US is well covered and the list was sorted worst-first.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, backlog as metric, depth as value
  from market.backlog_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and error is null
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Backlogs that could not be counted
panels.description: NULL depth is NOT zero. A view that has started timing out would read as drained if its failure were recorded as an empty result — the same confusion between 'refused' and 'has nothing' that this pipeline has hit six times. Anything appearing here needs looking at.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, backlog as metric, duration_ms as value
  from market.backlog_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and error is not null
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Run outcomes
panels.description: `skipped` is a SUCCESS — the TTL guard found the data fresh. But a resource that ONLY ever skips is not working, which is why the two are separate series rather than one 'ok'.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('hour', started_at) as time,
       case when not ok then 'failed' when skipped then 'skipped' else 'ran' end as metric,
       count(*) as value
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at)
 group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Rows written per resource
panels.description:
Throughput — but read it beside the backlog panel. A `written` that looks healthy while the backlog is flat means the page is not advancing: derive_security_metrics returned 'written: 7386' twice, byte-identical, doing the same work forever.

IT USED TO FILTER THE INFORMATIVE CASE AWAY. Measured 2026-08-28: that filter hid 53 runs across 7 resources — including security-corporate-actions, which sat at written=0 for seven consecutive runs while silently rate-limited. A throughput chart that cannot draw a zero cannot show a resource that stopped working. A panel that drops the zero row deletes exactly the state it exists to reveal — the same defect as the cross table's `limit 60`, which hid the United States because the US is well covered and the list was sorted worst-first.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('hour', started_at) as time, resource as metric, sum(written) as value
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at)
 group by 1, 2 order by 1

panels.title: Time since each resource last succeeded
panels.description: The pg_cron rotation gives each resource a turn every ~3.2 hours (38 resources, one every 5 minutes), so anything over 8 hours is two missed sweeps and is what the alert fires on. This previously said 'the warm-up runs every 3 hours, so anything over 12' — the GitHub workflow it described was deleted when the scheduler moved into the database.

targets.rawSql:
select resource,
       round(extract(epoch from (now() - max(finished_at) filter (where ok))) / 3600.0, 1)
         as "hours since ok",
       max(finished_at) filter (where ok) as "last success"
  from market.refresh_run
 where started_at > now() - interval '30 days'
 group by resource
 order by 2 desc nulls first

panels.title: Recent failures
panels.description: The reason, not just the fact. Since 2026-08-13 an application failure answers 200 with `ok:false`; a bare 502 with no body means the WORKER died — look at memory, not at error handling.

targets.rawSql:
select started_at as "when", resource, http_status as "http", left(error, 160) as error
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and not ok
 order by started_at desc limit 100

panels.title: Provider throttle pressure
panels.description: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, AND IT REPORTS GREEN EVERYWHERE ELSE. A throttled provider is not an error: it is a SUCCESSFUL run carrying a throttledOut flag, so 'Run outcomes' and 'Recent failures' both look healthy during it. Measured 2026-08-28: 4 errored runs in two days, ZERO with a throttle signature in the error text. http-cache cannot see it either, because yfinance calls made inside openbb-api never traverse it. This panel is the only view of the limit that governs the whole pipeline. Over-driving it once negative-cached ~8,300 securities as permanently unanswerable in a single afternoon. Note throttledOut is a BOOLEAN flag, not a count — it is counted as runs affected.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('hour', started_at) as time, resource || ' · throttled' as metric,
       count(*) filter (where (report->>'throttledOut')::boolean) as value
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and jsonb_typeof(report->'throttledOut') = 'boolean'
 group by 1, 2 having count(*) filter (where (report->>'throttledOut')::boolean) > 0
union all
select date_trunc('hour', started_at), resource || ' · batches failed',
       sum((report->>'batchesFailed')::bigint)
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and jsonb_typeof(report->'batchesFailed') = 'number'
 group by 1, 2 having sum((report->>'batchesFailed')::bigint) > 0
union all
select date_trunc('hour', started_at), resource || ' · cut by deadline',
       sum((report->>'skippedByDeadline')::bigint)
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and jsonb_typeof(report->'skippedByDeadline') = 'number'
 group by 1, 2 having sum((report->>'skippedByDeadline')::bigint) > 0
 order by 1

panels.title: Worker budget headroom — seconds used of the 90s limit
panels.description: Recorded on every run since migration 127 and plotted nowhere until now. The worker budget is 90s (ours, in functions/main/index.ts — not a platform ceiling). Measured 2026-08-28: security-performance p95 68.8s / max 70.2s, security-price-history 65.1s. security-performance has been KILLED before, and a killed worker never calls finish_refresh — it holds the in-flight lock for ~2 minutes, so the next call answers 'skipped: fresh or in flight' and reads as an ordinary TTL skip rather than wreckage. The 90s line turns that from a post-mortem into a prediction. Only resources above 20s are drawn; the rest are noise.

targets.rawSql:
select date_trunc('hour', started_at) as time, resource as metric,
       max(duration_ms) / 1000.0 as value
  from market.refresh_run
 where $__timeFilter(started_at) and duration_ms is not null
 group by 1, 2 having max(duration_ms) > 20000
 order by 1

panels.title: Scheduler (pg_cron)
panels.description: pg_cron is now the ONLY thing driving this pipeline, and its failure mode is silent: the data stops being refreshed while every count stays plausible for days. These metrics were being sampled and NO dashboard read them — an alert fired against a series with nothing to look at. ticks_1h should sit near 13 (12 rotation + 1 observability); minutes_since_tick above 30 means it has stopped.

targets.rawSql:
select sampled_at as time, metric, value
  from market.universe_sample
 where $__timeFilter(sampled_at) and metric like 'scheduler.%'
 order by sampled_at

panels.title: Backlog drain rate — is it moving, and is it moving for the right reason?
panels.description:
THE DERIVATIVE, WHICH IS THE SIGNAL `written` ONLY PRETENDS TO BE. Two live stalls were found by eye on 2026-08-28 — security-statements returned `written: 240, remaining: 8668` byte-identical on five consecutive runs. The depth was in backlog_sample the whole time and nothing computed a rate, so the chart drew a flat line and no alert could fire on 'flat'.

FLAT with a non-zero depth is the stall signature (seven occurrences). draining_by_marking is the 2026-08-13 signature, where a backlog empties by negative-caching rather than by working: ~8,300 securities were marked permanently unanswerable while every count read as progress. Its depth curve is IDENTICAL to a healthy drain — only the negative cache distinguishes them, which is why the two rates are shown together.

targets.rawSql:
select backlog, state, depth, per_day, cache_per_day, days_to_empty, samples
  from market.backlog_drain
 order by case state when 'draining_by_marking' then 0 when 'FLAT' then 1 when 'growing' then 2 else 3 end, depth desc

panels.title: Dagster lanes (ingestion that has left the edge)
Dagster runs by job
panels.description: Every job that ran in the time range, from Dagster's own run storage (the `muffin-dagster` datasource, read as `metrics_ro`). `max_wait_s` is the longest a run queued before starting: the company lane holds the `yfinance` AND `sql` pools from 03:30 to about 06:00, so the asset jobs created meanwhile (`__ASSET_JOB`, which includes `derived_security_metrics`) wait up to two hours, and that is expected. A run that SUCCEEDED proves nothing about its data: read its counters with `muffin-dagster-operations`.

targets.rawSql:
select pipeline_name as job,
       count(*) as runs,
       count(*) filter (where status = 'SUCCESS') as succeeded,
       count(*) filter (where status = 'FAILURE') as failed,
       count(*) filter (where status = 'CANCELED') as canceled,
       count(*) filter (where status not in ('SUCCESS', 'FAILURE', 'CANCELED')) as not_finished,
       max(create_timestamp) as last_created,
       round((percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by end_time - start_time)
              filter (where status = 'SUCCESS'))::numeric) as median_run_s,
       round(max(start_time - extract(epoch from create_timestamp))::numeric) as max_wait_s
  from runs
 where $__timeFilter(create_timestamp)
 group by 1
 order by 1

panels.title: Failed or cancelled Dagster runs
panels.description: Every run in the time range that did not succeed, with the tags that say why it exists. The reason a run failed is in the Dagster UI (or `scripts/run_events.py`), on its STEP_FAILURE or ENGINE_EVENT; a run the monitor ended shows `DagsterExecutionInterruptedError`, with the reason on its PIPELINE_FAILURE. The alert 'A Dagster run failed' fires for six hours after any row appears here.

targets.rawSql:
select r.create_timestamp as created, left(r.run_id, 8) as run, r.pipeline_name as job, r.status,
       (select t.value from run_tags t where t.run_id = r.run_id and t.key = 'muffin/reason') as reason,
       (select t.value from run_tags t where t.run_id = r.run_id and t.key = 'dagster/partition') as partition
  from runs r
 where $__timeFilter(r.create_timestamp)
   and r.status in ('FAILURE', 'CANCELED')
 order by r.create_timestamp desc

panels.title: Queue wait per run, by job (seconds)
panels.description: How long each run waited between being created and starting, one point per run. Pools are run-granularity, so a long run holds its pool for its whole length: the price night serialises its 100 runs on `yfinance` and `sql`, and the company lane holds both from 03:30. A wait that grows on a day nothing else changed is a pool held by something stuck: a run left STARTED after a roll holds its slot until it is failed by hand.

targets.rawSql:
select create_timestamp as time,
       pipeline_name as metric,
       round((start_time - extract(epoch from create_timestamp))::numeric) as value
  from runs
 where $__timeFilter(create_timestamp)
   and start_time is not null
 order by 1

panels.title: Asset checks: the latest evaluation of each, last 30 days
panels.description: Every Dagster asset check's most recent result, failures first, whatever the time range. `last_passed` separates a known state from news: `no_company_is_far_behind_the_rotation` reads ERROR until the company lane's first rotation completes (2026-10-24) and has never passed, while a check that passed last week and fails now has regressed, which is what the alert 'A Dagster asset check started failing' watches. WARN checks never alert. Checks evaluated in the last 30 days only, whatever the time picker says: Dagster keeps the history of checks on assets that were deleted (`raw_price_bars`, `ledger_health`), and without the window they would sit at the top for ever. A live check that stops being evaluated shows its age in `evaluated` long before it drops out.

targets.rawSql:
with latest as (
  select distinct on (asset_key, check_name)
         asset_key, check_name, execution_status, create_timestamp, evaluation_event
    from asset_check_executions
   where execution_status in ('SUCCEEDED', 'FAILED')
     and create_timestamp > (now() at time zone 'utc') - interval '30 days'
   order by asset_key, check_name, id desc)
select l.check_name as "check",
       trim(both '[]"' from l.asset_key) as asset,
       l.execution_status as status,
       replace(l.evaluation_event::json->'dagster_event'->'event_specific_data'->'severity'->>'__enum__',
               'AssetCheckSeverity.', '') as severity,
       l.create_timestamp as evaluated,
       (select max(p.create_timestamp) from asset_check_executions p
         where p.asset_key = l.asset_key and p.check_name = l.check_name
           and p.execution_status = 'SUCCEEDED') as last_passed
  from latest l
 order by (l.execution_status = 'FAILED') desc, l.check_name
